title: research: exclude eight calls for one GL3 dirty-register target
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The third-register probe in #1974 excluded savings through seven paid calls and left length eight open. This package excludes eight calls for the fixed direct-nine target
`diag([A],[B],[I])`, `A=(1,4,3)`, `B=(2,4,3)` in row-mask notation.

In the exact model `M3(F2[GL3(F2)])`, with an arbitrary third input restored exactly, this target has minimum nine paid calls. Each position ranges over all six coordinate-CNOT labels and all 28 binary rank-one idempotents: 168 allowed factors, with free scalar mixing normalized as in the predecessor. The encoding checks all full group-algebra coefficients.

The evidence is two saved CNFs with independently checked RUP proofs, a documented equivalence argument, and exact replay of the known direct-nine construction. The seven-call certificate reproduces prior coverage. The new scoped contribution is the eight-call exclusion. Involutivity and pair padding combine the seven/eight exclusions into a lower bound of nine.

This does not establish a new kappa, selected frontier, general integer-multiplication bound or physical implementation. The external proof checker certifies the CNFs; independent human review of their equivalence to the stated model remains outstanding.

## Task and overlap

- Scientific baseline and refreshed main: `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7.
- Predecessor #1974: `a4992da8e4e81a74cf1fd2b2d3af948662476d6e`. The relevant predecessor package trees are identical at these pins.
- [Claim posted before computation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2102#discussioncomment-19075155), scoped to this one target.
- Scope refined only by adding a seven-call control so the at-most-eight inference has its own certificate. No whole-family commitment.
- The earlier #2102 search was restricted to 25,125,000 two-bridge words; its outcome is unknown. This encoding removes those restrictions. The live pre-submission refresh covered 324 open PRs and 2,806 discussion records without warnings; targeted inspection found only the prior thread and this claim for the exact target. This is not a global novelty certificate.

## Validation

| Calls | CNF variables | Clauses | Uncompressed proof bytes | Original DRAT-trim result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 7 | 18,882 | 61,138 | 3,657,455 | `s VERIFIED`, 2.003 s |
| 8 | 30,591 | 97,770 | 108,920,783 | `s VERIFIED`, 164.347 s |

Accepted proofs came from Glucose4 through PySAT 1.9.dev17. The separate DRAT-trim checker is pinned at `2e3b2dc0ecf938addbd779d42877b6ed69d9a985`, run with `-U` to accept only RUP additions. Its unchanged source and MIT license are included; no executable is committed.

The [package README](https://github.com/brianross93/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ca0002008b497428f0b651501c4a220a9d2785e7/research/gl3-fixed-target-eight-call-pilot/README.md) gives full commands. From the package directory:

```sh
python -B verify.py
cc -std=c99 -O2 -Dgetc_unlocked=getc third_party/drat-trim/drat-trim.c -o third_party/drat-trim/drat-trim
python -B verify.py --proofs --checker third_party/drat-trim/drat-trim
```

[CERTIFICATES.json](https://github.com/brianross93/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ca0002008b497428f0b651501c4a220a9d2785e7/research/gl3-fixed-target-eight-call-pilot/CERTIFICATES.json) contains exact hashes and original checker records. The gzip payloads preserve the accepted proofs exactly. Fresh publication-package verification regenerates both CNFs and replays both proofs; the known nine-call word passes all 504 regular basis inputs. Controls cover all 168 factors, formal-vs-natural aliases, dirty-register restoration, Boolean gate equivalence, and fixed-word positive/negative cases.

The earlier native Z3 trace was rejected and contributes no proof credit. Its hash, size and diagnostics are retained in `FAILED_ATTEMPTS.json`; the unnecessary 182 MB failed trace and machine-specific logs are omitted. Timeouts are not treated as proofs. The first eight-call worker's peak memory is unknown because its original monitor sampled the Windows launcher; this limitation is disclosed.

No broad predecessor census, Lean proof, or full multiplication-theorem replay was run. This isolated package does not change shared code or the selected result. The remaining trust obligations are explicit in [ENCODING_AUDIT.md](https://github.com/brianross93/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ca0002008b497428f0b651501c4a220a9d2785e7/research/gl3-fixed-target-eight-call-pilot/ENCODING_AUDIT.md).

## Credit

Brian Ross contributed the conceptual search strategy, proposed transferring the constraint-search approach developed in his earlier Jane Street work, and provided research direction and oversight. Implementation, computational checks and documentation used substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The model and prior bounds build on Hanson Sun's seed18 package and Josie Elliston's length10 package and three-register probe. Their attribution is retained, together with the checker license.

## Open next questions

The smallest useful next step is an independent review of the encoding equivalence and support argument, followed by proof replay on another platform. A broader fixed-target campaign would require its own overlap check, scope and resource assessment. See the package's open questions; this PR does not claim to answer them.
